text.p: SOLIDERE shares fell in sharply reduced turnover for the second successive day on Tuesday as investors continued to take profits after a recent two-week surge.
A shares fell to $110.875 from $114 and B shares fell to $115.875 from $116.
The shares had rallied in the previous two weeks amid expectations that SOLIDERE will launch a $150 million GDR issue in October allowing non-Arab investors access to the market.

Turnover on the privately-operated Beirut Secondary Market (BSM), which trades only SOLIDERE shares, fell to 4,124 shares from 7,551 on Monday and 11,668 on Friday. Value was $465,508 compared with $878,948 on Monday and $1,362,200.5 on Friday.
There was no trade for the second successive day on the official Beirut Stock Exchange (BSE) in any of the listed companies: Ciments Libanais, Ciments Blancs, Eternit and Uniceramic.
The LISPI index fell 0.41 percent to 84.45. The BLOM stock index fell 1.53 percent to 968.94. Both indexes cover both markets.
